title: Five questions, asked before the deposit clears.
subtitle: After that the good cabins are gone and you are negotiating from the back of the queue.

text: Cabin choice is the one decision that gets worse every week you wait.
sub: Ships, fares and itineraries stay available for months. Position does not. The quiet midship cabins go first, and they go to whoever asked for them by name.

items.head: What is directly above and below?
items.body: Pool deck, galley, lounge, crew stair. Any of the four is a reason to move one deck.

items.head: Does it have a connecting door?
items.body: You inherit whoever is behind it. On the plan it is a small mark that is easy to miss.

items.head: Is the view qualified in any way?
items.body: Obstructed, partially obstructed, or overhung. All three are disclosed, in one quiet word.

items.head: How far along the hull is it?
items.body: Forward for the drama, midship for the sleep. Aft if the water on that route is kind.

items.head: Is it an accessible cabin?
items.body: Wider doors, a roll-in bathroom, and often a better position. Do not book one you don't need.

left.label: If you need it
items: Check the route to the lift

points.label: Twelve months out
points.value: The plan is open. Every quiet cabin and every good aft terrace is available.

points.label: Six months out
points.value: Midship goes first, then the accessible cabins, then the aft corners.

points.label: Inside ninety days
points.value: What remains is the guarantee pool, and the guarantee pool is what nobody chose.

points.label: Final fortnight
points.value: Fares may fall. Position will not come back. That is the whole trade.

text: Book the ship early for the cabin, not for the fare.
sub: Fares can be watched and repriced downwards after you book — I do it routinely. A cabin position cannot be recovered once the plan has filled. Secure the position; chase the price afterwards.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with.
body: Or send me the sailing you're considering and I'll come back with the cabins I'd take, the ones I'd refuse, and the reason for each. Complimentary.
